originality.rationale: A prior height-two exact census determines isolated individual values of the graph-incidence invariant, but does not state an all-order law relating edge attachments across parameter sets. The prior signed effect of adding a comparability is a distinct operation and does not imply strict positivity. Crown-Lucas ideal count and ideal/filter extension theory are explicit prior inputs. Searches did not locate an equivalent mixed-difference theorem; implicit coverage remains the main risk.
residual_risks: Published generic height-two formula directly determines individual t(E) values, so a reader may independently derive the mixed law as an implicit corollary; no published statement of positivity at all orders was found.
Unindexed literature on absolute monotonicity or graph lattice-gas partition functions may contain an equivalent all-order identity.
The hypergraph-induced polynomial article was inspected only at abstract level; it discusses a related but different polynomial and no random-poset invariant in its abstract.

value.rationale: The graph incidence poset is canonical and the question of edge-cell editing is mathematically natural. The finding settles the entire hierarchy of marginal interactions over an infinite graph family with a strict sign and explicit coefficients, beyond pointwise re-enumeration or routine numerical observations. It distinguishes addition of a parameter-cell from earlier addition of a relation and provides a usable exact positive support expansion.
